references.text: Confession of sin is required in connection with the guilt offering; the same principle applies to confessing the sin one has committed.
Describes restitution plus an additional fifth for the guilt offering; the same principle of full restitution plus twenty percent.
Confession of sin as a vital element in repentance and restoring the relationship with God.
Addition of a fifth upon redemption; the same principle of restitution with a twenty percent surcharge.
The continuation of this text explains what happens if there is no one to whom restitution can be made.
David confesses his sin to the Lord, an example of confession leading to forgiveness.
The one who confesses and turns away from their sins finds mercy.
The wicked shall restore what they have stolen; the principle of restitution for life.
People confessed their sins when baptized by John; confession as part of repentance.
Zacchaeus promises to give back fourfold to those he has defrauded; the principle of restitution in repentance.
Confess your sins to one another; a New Testament exhortation to confession.
If we confess our sins, God is faithful and righteous so that He forgives us our sins.
